desc:
A country has n cities labelled 0 to n - 1 and exactly n - 1 one-way roads. Each entry roads[i] = [a, b] is a road that can only be driven from city a to city b. If you ignore the directions, the roads connect all the cities and there is exactly one route between any two cities.

City 0 is the capital. You may reverse the direction of some roads so that, in the end, a traveller starting in any city can reach the capital. Return the minimum number of roads you must reverse.
constraints: Ignoring directions the roads form a tree (every city is connected to every other city)
hints: Because the roads form a tree, every city has exactly one route towards the capital. Which direction must each road on that route have?
Look at a road from the capital's side: it must point towards the parent (closer to city 0). If it points away from city 0, it has to be reversed.

Do a BFS or DFS from city 0 on the undirected tree. Store each road at both ends, with a cost of 1 when you traverse it in its original direction (that means it points away from city 0) and 0 otherwise. Sum the costs of the tree edges you use.
editorial: Turn the roads into an undirected adjacency list, remembering the original direction: the entry a → b stored at a carries cost 1 and the mirror entry stored at b carries cost 0. Now walk the tree outward from city 0. When you step from u to a new city v along an entry of cost 1, the road was built from u to v, i.e. away from the capital, so it must be reversed. Entries of cost 0 already point towards the capital.

Each road lies on the unique path of exactly one of its endpoints to the capital, and its required direction is fixed, so the reversals are forced and the sum of the costs is both necessary and enough. The traversal visits every city and road once, so it runs in O(n). An iterative traversal avoids recursion limits on a long chain.
solution:
def minReorder(n, roads):
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for a, b in roads:
        adj[a].append((b, 1))
        adj[b].append((a, 0))
    seen = [False] * n
    seen[0] = True
    stack = [0]
    flips = 0
    while stack:
        u = stack.pop()
        for v, cost in adj[u]:
            if not seen[v]:
                seen[v] = True
                flips += cost
                stack.append(v)
    return flips
